title: multiregion-policy-override-notes
content:
Context:
- Small production incident (2026-02-27 22:14 UTC) where traffic intended for eu-west-1 was observed getting routed to us-west-2 for a subset of API keys from a single customer. Customer saw elevated latency and some 504s when their requests hit us-west-2 model variant (different quantization).
- Post-incident: we reverted an emergency override that had been applied earlier in the day. Suspect the override had unexpectedly high precedence vs. region affinity policy.

What I observed (raw breadcrumbs):
- Spike graph (console) shows increased P50/P99 at 22:13 UTC for route /v1/generate for model-id redwood/open-13b-8bit in eu-west-1 tenant=acme-inc.
- Telemetry: routing.policy_eval logs: "policy=region_affinity,score=0.92" then immediately "policy=override_match,score=1.0,override_id=ovrd-2026-02-27-19" then decision=route:us-west-2.
- Trace sample (trace id 01cf...): routing->cache-lookup failed (ttl mismatch), fallback to global pool, then enforcement of override.

Repro attempts run locally (notes):
- Replayed a small batch using simple curl with test key (on staging):
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test' -d '{"model":"redwood/open-13b-8bit","input":"hello"}' | jq .
  => route chosen = eu-west-1 (expected).
- Replayed with header override (x-rw-override: ovrd-2026-02-27-19) -> route chosen = us-west-2 (expected for override).
- Replayed with same override but with lower TTL in policy cache (simulate stale): forced policy cache to return older policy (see commands below) -> route chosen = us-west-2.

Commands / env used while probing: (rough, executed on staging cluster controller)
- kubectl -n routing logs svc-policy-engine-67c9f7b6 -c policy-engine --since=2h | grep ovrd-2026-02-27 || true
- redis-cli -h cache-router.prod get policy:ovrd-2026-02-27 || true
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/internal/policy/evaluate -H 'Authorization: Bearer internal-key' -d '{"key":"sk-acme-123","route":"/v1/generate","region_hint":"eu-west-1"}'
- tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/routing-probe.pcap port 443 & (used during a live replay to capture egress ip)

Error snippets and oddities captured:
- policy-engine logs:
  "WARN policy-eval: override matched but ttl_expired=false, precedence=1000, note="unexpected precedence over affinity""
- route-router logs:
  "INFO route-decision: selected=us-west-2, available=[eu-west-1,us-west-2], reason=override-match"
- A handful of 504s with error:
  "upstreamTimeout: handshake to model host timed out (us-west-2-pool-03), retries=2"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) The emergency override (ovrd-2026-02-27-19) was applied with global scope and a higher precedence value than region_affinity, and policy-engine evaluation didn't tie-break by region latency when override present. This is intended for manual quick fixes but operator set precedence too high.
2) Policy cache TTL staleness + async policy push: some edge controllers had an older override state (e.g., still active) while others had the reverted state leading to inconsistent routing.
3) A race during override rollback where the rollback API acknowledged quickly but the on-disk store (redis) updated later; some controllers fetched the old override before the rollback completed.
4) Servo: a bug in the comparator: comparator treats override precedence as absolute number and doesn't consider rule scope (global vs. region).

Evidence for/against each:
- Evidence for (1): override precedence logged as 1000 (very high) and decision shows override-match.
- Evidence for (2): staggered last_modified timestamps in /config/policies across controllers (one controller had last_modified 2026-02-27T19:03:01Z while others 2026-02-27T19:03:12Z).
- Evidence for (3): redis monitored ops showed HSET ovrd-2026-02-27:status -> "removed" at 19:04:00 but some controllers still returned get(policy:ovrd-2026-02-27) -> JSON with active=true for ~8s after.
- Evidence for (4): code review TODOs in the comparator suggest scope-awareness not fully implemented (see linked PR).

Quick mitigation done during incident (what we tried):
- Rolled back ovrd-2026-02-27-19 at 19:04 (api acknowledged).
- Disabled override precedence by setting precedence=0 in policy-engine (emergency hotfix) to force region_affinity to win.
- Throttled new policy pushes for 10m to observe stability.
- Manually rebalance some sessions in us-west-2 to reduce queued work and lower 504s.

What didn't help / surprising results:
- Re-pushing the same policy after rollback didn't immediately fix all controllers. Shows eventual consistency window ~10s.
- Some logs show override-match even when cache reported override removed (race).

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- Add a short-term guardrail: disallow precedence > 500 for overrides with global scope (policy-engine validation). (owner: Diego)
- Add a confirm-sync step to rollback API: write the rollback to redis and wait for acks from N control-plane replicas before returning 200 (owner: Lena). Risk: increases rollback latency, but safer.
- Instrumented telemetry: emit policy_version header in routing decisions for correlation (owner: me).
- Postmortem: capture exact affected customer keys and estimate exposure window (owner: SRE oncall).

Longer-term fixes / design changes to consider:
- Make overrides region-scoped by default unless explicitly global. This reduces blast radius.
- Introduce a policy precedence matrix: some policies (SLA-driven region_affinity) should always be able to override overrides in the event of SLO breach.
- Rework comparator logic so precedence is a tuple: (scope_rank, numeric_precedence, timestamp) so we avoid absolute overrides trumping scoped rules.
- Improve policy push to use CAS or versioned config plus backoff to reduce transient mismatch between controllers.

Notes to self / experiments to run in staging:
- Create a test override with global scope precedence 900 and measure time to full propagation under varying k (replica count).
- Simulate rollback storms: apply + rollback 10x in 30s and watch cache divergence.
- Test 'confirm-sync' approach by instrumenting rollback API to wait for quorum ack (start with quorum=2).

Quick snippets to repro behavior on staging (unsafe; internal only):
- Apply override (internal API):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/internal/policy/overrides -H 'Authorization: Bearer internal-key' -d '{"id":"ovrd-test-1","scope":"global","precedence":900,"match":{"api_key":"sk-acme-123"}}'
- Rollback:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/internal/policy/overrides/ovrd-test-1/rollback -H 'Authorization: Bearer internal-key'
- Check controller cache:
  kubectl -n routing exec controller-0 -- redis-cli GET policy:ovrd-test-1 | jq .

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should rollback API be synchronous by default or opt-in?
- What's acceptable rollback latency given common operational workflows?
- Can we detect "override storm" and automatically cap precedence temporarily?

Random notes / observations:
- Customer had occasional small packet-loss on their peering into eu-west-1 that day (Slack thread #network-peering). Could add noise to affinity scoring but not primary cause.
- Need to update runbook: list override_id and who applied it in every emergency action. We had an ambiguous audit entry.

References and links (temp):
- Slack: #oncall-routing thread ts=2026-02-27T19:08Z
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/814 (comparator TODO)
- Jira: JIRA-4821 (postmortem ticket)

End of notes.

Signed-off: Asha (quick personal scratchpad, will formalize for postmortem)
summary: Incident scratchpad capturing commands, logs, hypotheses, and action items for a multiregion routing override that led to unexpected traffic egress to a remote region. Draft for postmortem.
